justifications.r1: Dense 1- and 2-CMC ramp suite (dorks, Nature's Lore, Talismans) paired with token mana engines (Jaheira, Inspiring Statuary, Ninja Pizza).
justifications.r2: Continuous symmetrical exile card flow on every player's end step via Rocco, supported by Peregrin Took, Baylen, and Inspiring Call.
justifications.a1: High redundancy of Food creators and exile-matters payoffs, though lacking dedicated creature tutors.
justifications.a2: Engine comes online consistently by Turn 3 with a Turn 2 or 3 Rocco deployment.
justifications.p1: Presents lethal combat overruns or machine-gun burn by Turn 5 via Night of the Sweets' Revenge, Shalai and Hallar, and All Will Be One.
justifications.p2: Requires 2 opponent response cycles to close out games through combat damage or incremental counter burn.
justifications.p3: Impulse exile plays reveal drawn cards to the entire table, giving opponents advance telegraphing.
justifications.i1: Premier instant-speed removal suite (Swords, Path, Beast Within, Chaos Warp, Delayed Blast Fireball, Blasphemous Act, Farewell).
justifications.i2: Completely devoid of stax, taxing effects, or resource denial (F tier).
justifications.s1: Moderate protection suite including Inspiring Call, Bolt Bend, Deflecting Palm, and Plaza of Heroes.
justifications.s2: Food tokens remain on the battlefield through board wipes, allowing instant re-activation of engines and life buffer.
justifications.s3: Engine pieces like Baylen, Jaheira, Academy Manufactor, and Killer Service operate effectively without Rocco on board.

overview: This Rocco, Street Chef deck is an aggressive Naya Food and exile-matters midrange strategy. It establishes its primary engine early by casting Rocco on Turn 2 or 3, generating continuous card advantage and token creation whenever cards are played from exile. The deck converts Food tokens and +1/+1 counters into explosive mana and card flow using key enablers like Jaheira, Friend of the Forest, Academy Manufactor, and Baylen, the Haymaker. Without relying on infinite combos, it closes games through overwhelming combat damage and burn, utilizing overrun effects like Night of the Sweets' Revenge alongside direct damage engines such as Shalai and Hallar and All Will Be One. The deck features robust removal and high card velocity, though it remains vulnerable to mass exile wipes and provides symmetrical card access to opponents.

core_strategy: Accelerate mana on Turns 1–2 using one-drop dorks or two-drop ramp spells to cast Rocco, Street Chef ahead of curve.
Deploy Rocco on Turn 2 or 3 to begin exiling cards on end steps, triggering +1/+1 counters and Food creation on subsequent turns.
Leverage token converters like Academy Manufactor, Jaheira, Friend of the Forest, and Peregrin Took to turn Food into massive mana and card velocity.
Close the game on Turns 5–7 using massive overrun attacks via Night of the Sweets' Revenge, giant unblockable threats like Feasting Hobbit, or direct burn from All Will Be One and Shalai and Hallar.

keep: Hands with 2–3 lands, at least one 1- or 2-mana ramp piece to cast Rocco, Street Chef on Turn 2 or 3, and a token payoff or interaction spell.
avoid: Hands lacking green mana, hands with only expensive 4+ mana payoffs and no early acceleration, or hands without colored fixing for Naya.

key_tips: Prioritize casting spells from exile over hand spells to trigger Rocco, Street Chef and grow your creatures with +1/+1 counters.
Save Delayed Blast Fireball to cast from exile via Rocco or foretell, turning it into a one-sided 5-damage board wipe.
Use Inspiring Call or Plaza of Heroes reactively to protect your key engine pieces against opposing destroy wipes and spot removal.

critical: Heavy reliance on creature and artifact permanents makes the board vulnerable to comprehensive sweepers like Farewell or Vandalblast.
Lack of stack interaction or counterspells leaves the deck exposed to fast opposing combo wins.
moderate: Symmetrical card access from Rocco, Street Chef can hand opponents answers or acceleration if they utilize exile cards effectively.
Absence of creature tutors requires relying on draw velocity to find specific finishers like All Will Be One.
minor: Targeted removal on Rocco before the end step delays initial token production and counter distribution.
